svg.title: Confirming a Real Download, End to End
svg.desc: A four-row stack. Row 1: filtered, a real pandas DataFrame built from the selectbox. Row 2: csv_bytes, filtered.to_csv().encode() -- the exact bytes st.download_button would hand to the browser. Row 3: a real round-trip check, decoding those exact bytes back with pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(csv_bytes)) and confirming rows, columns, and values all match the original filtered DataFrame exactly. Row 4: AppTest confirms the on-screen table -- built from the identical filtered variable -- correctly shows 52 rows for Africa and 2 for Oceania, indirect but real proof the download reflects the current filter.
svg.text: Confirming a Real Download, End to End
filtered -- a real pandas DataFrame, built from the selectbox
csv_bytes = filtered.to_csv().encode() -- the exact download bytes
AppTest confirms the on-screen table: 52 rows (Africa), 2 rows (Oceania)
The download button itself has no readable bytes through AppTest -- confirmed instead by round-
tripping the identical bytes directly, and by checking the on-screen table that shares the same
